observed: The central box is subtitled 'append K/V / one step later' and receives arrows from all four left-column tokens, including token1 'end of prefill'. page_hint: Ch 1 §1 'Concept' — 'Attention' subsection, paragraph introducing the three-row attention-architecture taxonomy table
quoted_clause: The canonical three-row taxonomy, used by name in Ch. 3, Ch. 7 and Appendix A rather than re-described there: [...] This is why "the KV problem" and its fixes are really a *model-architecture* question (Ch. 3) that lands as a *memory* question (Ch. 7) — and why the token layer is the right place to have met it. observed: Ch 1 defers the GQA/MQA/MLA mechanism inventory to Ch 3, but Ch 3 as written does not deliver it. Ch 3's Concept section is about parameter allocation (dense vs MoE) plus the alternative-inference aside; GQA, MQA and MLA appear only in passing inside the KV discussion of §3 ('MLA-style latent attention does not stop the growth: it cuts the bytes/token constant (~50–60x for DeepSeek-class geometry)'). There is no attention-architecture section, no head-sharing mechanism, no latent-compression mechanism, and no explanation of why GQA/MQA reduce bytes while MLA changes the stored representation. The reader is told a promised mechanism inventory is coming and it never arrives in the chunk.
correction: Either (a) add a Ch 3 subsection 'Attention architecture and the KV constant' that gives the mechanism inventory Ch 1 promises — head sharing (GQA/MQA: one KV head serving G query heads; bytes/token scales as 1/G), latent compression (MLA: store the compressed latent d_c plus the decoupled rope part d_h^R instead of per-head K/V), and constant-state recurrent layers (Mamba/linear attention: fixed-size state, no per-token term) — with the byte formulas and one worked geometry each; or (b) rewrite Ch 1's deferral to point at Ch 7 (where the arithmetic lives) and at Appendix A, and drop the claim that Ch 3 holds the mechanism inventory. Option (a) is preferable: Ch 3's own §3 already needs the GQA/MQA/MLA distinction to justify the 'shape, not routing' argument.
acceptance_test: A reader who has read Ch 1 and Ch 3 can explain, in mechanism terms and without consulting Ch 7, why GQA/MQA shrink bytes/token, why MLA shrinks them by a different mechanism, and why neither stops linear growth; and no chapter promises a 'mechanism inventory' that another chapter does not contain.
verdict_evidence: ch01:43,:69 mechanism inventory 'Ch. 3's'; Ch3 has no attention-architecture section; MLA absent book-wide (grep never hits ch07, whose :88-98 covers GQA only).
fix_instruction: Add a Ch 3 or Ch 7 subsection on GQA/MQA (1/G bytes) and MLA (latent d_c + rope part), or retarget ch01:43/:69 to Ch 7.
